title: Remainder that follows the divisor
description: Divide a by b with the quotient q rounded down toward negative infinity, and return the remainder r = a - b*q. Because of the rounding, r is 0 or has the same sign as b. For example a = -7, b = 2 gives q = -4 and r = 1; a = 7, b = -2 gives q = -4 and r = -1. b is never 0 and may be negative.
notes: Experiment int_division: hidden tests use negative operands; the description states floor semantics (round toward negative infinity) in words. The ref.zehn is written with int.div_floor / int.div_trunc / int.rem_euclid so it is valid under int_ops=operators and int_ops=explicit.
